title: Effective Interest Rate vs. Nominal Interest Rate
description: Calculate the relationship between effective and nominal interest rates. The nominal interest rate is typically expressed per year, while the effective interest rate applies to sub-periods like months, weeks, or days. Use this tool to convert between nominal and effective interest rates.

components.content:
## Effective Interest Rate vs. Nominal Interest Rate

An interest rate is only meaningful in the context of time - typically understood as _per year_ (the **nominal interest rate**). With other periods of time like _month_, _week_, or _day_ - the rate may be called the **effective interest rate**.

### Formula 1: Nominal Interest Rate
_i = (1 + ie)^n - 1_

Where:
- **i** = nominal interest rate for the period
- **ie** = effective interest rate for the sub-period
- **n** = number of sub-periods

### Formula 2: Effective Interest Rate
_ie = (1 + i)^(1/n) - 1_

Where:
- **ie** = effective interest rate for sub-periods
- **i** = nominal interest rate for the period
- **n** = number of sub-periods
